reply.text:
Good on you for wanting to bring him in. For an 11-year-old, the training that matters most is simple: learn good movement first, keep the load light enough that every rep looks clean, and make it fun enough that he wants to come back. Bodyweight work like squats, push-ups on the knees or floor, lunges, hip hinges and carries, a few sets each, two or three days a week, covers it well. Some light lifting with a broomstick or very light dumbbells to learn bracing and form is fine too, with you watching every rep. Keep sessions short, around 30 to 40 minutes, and let him stop a set when his form breaks down rather than pushing for a number.

If you want, I can build him a short beginner program for the days you train together. Tell me how many days a week you're both free, and whether he has any equipment at home, and I'll set it up. And if he has any pain or a past injury, that one goes to his doctor or a physio before the gym.
